source_name: kif.gov.hu — Közadat / KIK data-supply portal (NISZ)
why_relevant: Operator-side portal for the Central Information Public Data Registry; documents which organisations are in scope, the reporting data model and the submission schedule. Useful for judging completeness and lag of kozadat.hu records before treating them as evidence of a bank/payments deal.

source_name: EKR – Ajánlatkérő nyilvántartás (register of contracting authorities)
why_relevant: Authoritative list of registered contracting authorities — the way to confirm which of MNB, Kincstár, MFB, EXIM, Posta, KELER, GIRO, Diákhitel are formally ajánlatkérő and under which regime (classic vs utility), and to snowball to further state-influenced financial buyers we have not named.

source_name: Nyilvántartott ajánlatkérők (register of contracting authorities)
why_relevant: Authoritative actor map: the full list of entities legally obliged to procure under Kbt. Used to build the target universe (ministries, municipalities, state holdings, utilities) whose banking/payments contracts must eventually be tendered.

source_name: KBA - Közbeszerzési Adatbázis (legacy pre-2018 procedures and contracts)
why_relevant: Historical archive of procedures and contracts before the EKR/CoRe cut-over (pre-2018). Needed to reconstruct multi-cycle history of bank account-management and card-acceptance mandates, which typically run on 3-5 year cycles.

source_name: Minősített ajánlattevők jegyzéke (qualified bidders list)
why_relevant: Supply-side map: which vendors are pre-qualified to bid. Combined with Kizárt ajánlattevők (excluded bidders) and Szerződésszegések (contract breaches) it profiles the competitive field around payments/IT contracts.

source_name: MNB törzsadat-bejelentés jogszabály (58/2015. MNB rendelet) és Intézménykereső / ERA
why_relevant: The master-data reporting regime (58/2015. MNB rendelet, submitted via the ERA portal) and the public institution search let you resolve exact legal entity identities of all banks in this cell and detect subsidiaries/outsourcing entities that are the real contracting parties for supplier deals.

source_name: MNB Piaci szereplők keresése (market participant search hub)
why_relevant: Landing hub linking all MNB register sub-searches (general search, intermediaries, special databases). Best single entry point for snowballing to every MNB-held list of actors.

source_name: MNB pénzforgalmi intézmény licensing guidance (engedélyezési útmutatók)
why_relevant: Defines the taxonomy of licence types and activity scopes used across every MNB register — needed to interpret register fields correctly and to build the local-language glossary for downstream cells.

source_name: Portfolio Banking Technology konferencia – Támogatók (sponsor pages, multi-year)
why_relevant: The flagship Hungarian bank-IT conference publishes tiered sponsor lists (Platinum/Super Gold/Gold/Silver/Bronze, professional and media partners) plus speaker-company rosters, per year since ~2017. Sponsor tiers are a paid, ranked signal of which vendors (e.g. 4iG, Accenture, adesso) are actively selling into Hungarian banks — a longitudinal supplier-intensity series for A2 tender targeting.

source_name: TED CPV browse (browse by sector) — banking/financial CPV families
why_relevant: Provides the controlled vocabulary anchor for the whole cell: CPV 66100000 banking and investment services, 66110000 banking services, 66172000 financial transaction processing / clearing-house services, 66600000 treasury services, plus adjacent IT CPVs (72200000, 48000000) that carry core-banking / card-system procurements.

source_name: Magyar Bankszövetség – Tagjaink (member list)
why_relevant: Authoritative roster of ~40+ Hungarian banks, mortgage banks, building societies and affiliated bodies (OTP, MBH, K&H, Erste, Raiffeisen, UniCredit, CIB, Gránit, MFB, KELER, Garantiqa, Magyar Lízingszövetség as affiliate). This is the canonical buyer-side universe for A2 tender/procurement monitoring: every entity here is a potential contracting authority or publisher of award notices.

entity_name: Magyar Fintech Szövetség / Hungarian Fintech Association
source_name: Magyar Fintech Szövetség / Hungarian Fintech Association (HFA) – Membership
why_relevant: MAFISZ/HFA aggregates the Hungarian fintech supplier ecosystem (startups, scale-ups, incubators, PSPs) that sells into banks. Membership roster enumerates likely bidders/subcontractors on Hungarian bank and payments tenders — a supplier map no public register holds.

entity_name: Magyar Fintech Szövetség / Hungarian Fintech Association
source_name: Hungarian Fintech Association (HFA / hunfintech.com) member directory
why_relevant: Curated directory of Hungarian fintech and banking-software companies with per-member profile pages describing clients and product lines. The single fastest way to expand the actor map of local fintech dev shops that subcontract to or compete with the large integrators.

source_name: karrierportal.hu - shared white-label ATS hosting Hungarian bank career sites
why_relevant: Multiple Hungarian financial institutions run their career sites on <company>.karrierportal.hu subdomains (observed: mkb, giro). Enumerating the subdomain pattern yields a low-noise, first-party hiring feed set for the whole sector.

entity_name: EIB Project Procurement guidance + Guide to Procurement
source_name: EIB Project Procurement guidance + Guide to Procurement (PDF)
why_relevant: Defines that EIB-financed promoters must publish notices in the OJEU/TED and, where applicable, on the EIB website — i.e. tells the collector exactly which downstream feeds carry EIB-driven Hungarian contracts.

source_name: FinTechZone – FinTechShow / BankTechShow / TechShow X. event pages
why_relevant: FinTechShow (Budapest Congress Center, ~80+ solutions in the exhibition gallery) and its successor TechShow X. publish tiered sponsor categories (Főszponzor, Arany/Ezüst/Bronz fokozatú szponzor, Kiemelt támogató, Megoldáspartner, Főtámogató) and speaker rosters. The exhibitor gallery is effectively a curated catalogue of vendors actively selling to Hungarian financial institutions.

source_name: IVSZ – Digitális Vállalkozások Szövetsége, tagvállalatok
why_relevant: IVSZ is Hungary's dominant ICT industry association; its member directory lists the IT integrators, software houses and consultancies (with membership-since dates) that bid on bank and public-sector IT tenders. Directly enumerates the vendor pool behind Hungarian financial-sector procurement.

source_name: K-Monitor main site — projects and activities index
why_relevant: Enumerates K-Monitor's data products (Adatbázis, Háló/aHáló network database, RedFlags, work on the Közadat register) and its analyses of the quality of the new state contract database — a shortcut to the whole Hungarian contract-transparency toolchain.

source_name: KiMitTud – FOI request archive (EUTAF and other audit bodies)
why_relevant: Public archive of freedom-of-information requests and the authorities' answers. Where audit/remedy documents are not proactively published, past FOI answers are often the only public route, and the archive shows what a given body has already released.

source_name: Tender Help Hungary
why_relevant: Bilingual HU/EN bid-support firm whose site maintains a 'tendering interfaces' page mapping TED, EKR and the Hungarian notice systems. Best used as a pointer source: it documents the plumbing of Hungarian procurement publication and explains which interface carries which notice type, which accelerates building the A2 source graph.

source_name: AmCham Hungary – Membership directory & Patron members
why_relevant: 300+ member companies with sector tagging, including banks (UniCredit, Raiffeisen), global IT vendors (IBM, T-Systems, Google, HP) and asset managers. Patron-member tiers reveal the highest-spend corporate players in Hungary — a bilingual, sector-filterable supplier/buyer directory plus an archived historical snapshot for change analysis.

source_name: Beszerzes.hu – Hungarian procurement-profession portal (beszállítók minősítése)
why_relevant: Hungarian procurement trade portal that surfaced repeatedly on supplier-qualification queries; useful for local vocabulary, prevailing supplier-qualification practice, and for identifying procurement leaders/consultancies serving Hungarian banks — a snowballing route to named procurement contacts.

source_name: Beszerzesi.info - tenderértesítő / tender hírlevél overview
why_relevant: Hungarian procurement-trade article enumerating tenderértesítő / tender hírlevél services and the vocabulary around them. Valuable as a snowball pointer: it is written in the practitioner's own terminology and names services that generic search does not rank, helping extend the HU glossary for this cell.

source_name: Budapest Fintech Week (Luma / Fintech.hu listings)
why_relevant: Umbrella week of Hungarian fintech side-events; the Luma listing and Fintech.hu tag page enumerate organisers, hosts and partner companies — a route into smaller vendors and hubs that never appear on the big-conference sponsor tiers.

entity_name: DUIHK / Német-Magyar Ipari és Kereskedelmi Kamara
source_name: DUIHK / Német-Magyar Ipari és Kereskedelmi Kamara – Tagság (member directory)
why_relevant: ~900 member companies — the largest bilateral business association in Hungary — with an online member directory. Captures German-owned banks, payment processors and IT suppliers operating in Hungary that other Hungarian-only rosters miss. Bilingual (hu/de/en) site.

source_name: e-Justice EU Business Registers — Hungary (BRIS gateway)
why_relevant: EU-level gateway describing and linking the Hungarian company register; useful for cross-border resolution of foreign parents of HU banking/payments vendors and for confirming the authoritative register endpoints.

source_name: Government Transparency Institute (GTI) — procurement datasets and methodology
why_relevant: Hungarian research institute that maintains Opentender and publishes the indicator methodology plus derived datasets and papers on Hungarian procurement concentration. Points to further datasets and to academic contacts who hold cleaned HU contract data.

source_name: i40platform.hu – szervezet/tagok (Industry 4.0 platform member organisations)
why_relevant: A state-linked platform whose member list includes IVSZ and DUIHK; it aggregates associations and companies in one place, which is a useful cross-index for discovering further Hungarian trade bodies relevant to digital and financial-sector procurement.

source_name: Infoklaszter (IT cluster) member company directory
why_relevant: Hungarian IT cluster listing member companies with capability descriptions. Complements HFA by covering integration/dev shops that are not fintech-branded but subcontract on banking and public-sector IT work.

source_name: Jorpex
why_relevant: Modern alerting service aggregating TED plus 50+ procurement portals with delivery to email or Slack. Its per-source documentation pages are themselves a pointer asset - they enumerate which national portals are indexed, useful for validating whether Hungarian sources beyond TED are genuinely covered.

source_name: kartyapiac.hu – Kártyapiac conference programme site
why_relevant: Dedicated microsite referenced by the organiser as carrying the continuously updated Kártyapiac programme; likely host of the current-year speaker, partner and exhibitor lists for Hungary's main card/payments event.

source_name: Magyar Lízingszövetség – Kik vagyunk / Bizottságok
why_relevant: 36 member asset-finance companies (leasing firms, banks, financial enterprises) financing ~500k individuals and 200k businesses. An adjacent-sector buyer list for payments/IT procurement, and its committee structure names the active practitioner network. Also an affiliate member of Magyar Bankszövetség (cross-link confirmed).

source_name: Mastercard payment facilitator directory
why_relevant: Scheme-maintained list of registered payment facilitators; filtering for Hungary-registered entities reveals PayFacs operating under HU acquirers — actors invisible in MNB registers because they ride an acquirer's licence.

source_name: MKIK – Magyar Kereskedelmi és Iparkamara (chamber registration & sections)
why_relevant: Chamber registration is mandatory for Hungarian businesses (membership is not), so the chamber system holds a near-complete registry of economic operators, searchable by county, town, activity and name. Useful for resolving and enriching supplier identities found in tender award notices, and its tagozatok (sections) map sectoral organisation.

source_name: MKIK 'Vállalkozz Digitálisan' accredited supplier catalogue (DIMOP Plusz)
why_relevant: Under DIMOP Plusz calls, digital tools and services (including POS/payment-adjacent hardware and software) must be bought from an accredited supplier catalogue maintained by the Hungarian Chamber of Commerce - effectively a pre-qualified vendor register and a demand-side pipeline for SME payment terminal deployments.

source_name: NAIH — általános közzétételi lista / 3.4 'Öt millió forint feletti szerződések' model page
why_relevant: The data-protection and FOI authority's own disclosure page shows the canonical structure and heading path ('III. Gazdálkodási adatok' → '3.4') that virtually every Hungarian public body reuses. That fixed path is the key to writing a generic crawler that finds any body's 5 M Ft contract list, including those of banks' public-sector clients. NAIH is also the appeal body when disclosure is refused.

source_name: openprocurements.com – Hungarian buyer profiles (hu.openprocurements.com)
why_relevant: Third-party mirror organised by BUYER, which is the axis this cell needs (per-hospital, per-university, per-municipality procurement history). Handy for quickly enumerating a buyer's past financial-services contracts.

source_name: Smartsector referenciák (HU financial-sector IT vendor)
why_relevant: Hungarian-language vendor reference page naming financial-sector clients; representative of a whole tier of small domestic suppliers whose 'referenciáink' pages are the only public record of their bank contracts.

source_name: TendersGo (Hungary opportunities)
why_relevant: Vendor content describing an AI-summarisation tender alert product with unlimited Hungary email alerts. Recorded as a pointer because the product's own canonical domain was not confirmed in this pass - only a marketing article on gtbc.net was observed. Worth resolving because AI-summarised tender documents would materially cut analyst effort on Hungarian-language specifications.
